utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Glavas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I wish a good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good morning, Mr. Glavas.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, at page 92, lines 10 through 12, speaking about the departure of the civilian Muslim population before the conflict broke out, you mentioned that this happened at the orders of the Crisis Staff. Did you mean the Muslim Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I meant the Bosniak Crisis Staff in Hadzici municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone ask you, either here or at the Bosnia-Herzegovina court, ask you about the structure and existence of the Muslim Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I correct if I say that Muslim Crisis Staffs were established and became operational as early as mid or the latest September 1991?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the Serbian Crisis Staff was established sometime in late March 1992, after the Muslims reneged on the agreement and --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I think it may have even been later. I think it may have been formed after the all-Serb Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to your own municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P2297, please, in e-court? This is a document dated 11 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, yesterday or the first day of your testimony, this was admitted into evidence as a document on the establishment of an advisory organ of Hadzici Serb Municipal Assembly, dated 11th April 1992. You mentioned that the civilian population there was unprepared and that they considered that they were actually left to their own means by the leadership; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Sarajevo, outside Hadzici municipality, for six days already, war had broken out, six days earlier?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In my earlier testimony, I've already said that we were rather late in all -- to follow up on all these events, the establishment of or the division of the police, breakout of the conflict and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your testimony and statements you mentioned the murder of a Serb policeman on the 4th of April. May I just remind you that this man's name was Petrovic, he was a police officer, and he was killed while he was on duty at the police station in the Novo Sarajevo Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am well aware of that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't recall seeing reference in any testimony or statement of Mr. Glavas to this effect and I just wonder if I could have a source for that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the reference, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did confirm this, and it would take up a lot of my time but I'm pretty certain that during the examination-in-chief he did mention the killing of this police officer. However, since that was not explored, I wanted to ask him whether that policeman was a Serb and whether this happened after mobilisation was declared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we proceed in the meantime? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that Mr. Izetbegovic on the 4th of April declared general mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 2 of this document, please, in English? We can leave the Serb as it is. Here we see that it says that on the 11th of April, it was decided that a body, a commission, should be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that commission's task would be? What the purpose of its establishment was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what commission you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me remind you, was the basic topic here the political and security situation in Hadzici municipality in this document, and then the second item on the agenda was miscellaneous issues?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here it says that Ratko Radic from the Serbian Territorial Defence and an army unit -- I can't find that in Serbian -- [In English] "Serbian Territorial Defence and an army unit needs to act together. The Serbian population needs to be protected from all possible attacks." [No interpretation]. [In English] "It is necessary to get organised as soon as possible to protect the population." [Interpretation] Was it only then that the people of Hadzici began considering this issue of protection and defence in the event of war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the topic we discussed, how to organise ourselves in Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if we keep ongoing, we see that Nevenko Samoukovic says that the municipal assembly and authorities are not functioning and he mentions that -- can we have the next page in Serbian, please. It is not legible enough, but basically what it says there is that the authorities and organisations are not functional; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's how it was in 1991, practically the assemblies were held without Serbian representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3247, please? 1D3247. We are not sure whether we have a translation. Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under item 1 here, does it say that at this session of 11th April, organs and bodies of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Hadzici were -- have been constituted and then it goes on to mention what the organs are. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's correct. And I believe I've already discussed this and answered questions about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now take a look, after bullets A and B, where it says: "All the activities above, and taken by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Hadzici, in order to protect the Serbian people and preserve peace in the territory of Hadzici municipality." And then -- is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then in the last paragraph it says: "The Assembly of the Serbian People of Hadzici wishes to take this opportunity to call on all the inhabitants of Hadzici municipality to preserve peace and refrain from doing anything that might harm somebody else, and it also stresses that all the three people -- that the assembly wishes to emphasise that it will strictly abide by all the republican decisions by the three peoples aimed at solving the current crisis." Is that what is stated there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this document admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1066, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3248, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from the news agency "SRNA" and this is a public proclamation. The police of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici, near Sarajevo, has incessantly been capturing Muslim terrorists. In addition to the three men of two days ago, of which we've informed you, last night 14 others were captured at Veljko Polje on Mount Igman, and again, a vehicle was captured, a refrigerated truck, and then it says what the registration plates are, and then it says where a quantity of ammunition and weapons was found. Then it goes on to say, "Za dom spremni." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a greeting used by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From what period, Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the time of the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that an Ustasha greeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So registration of the vehicle was -- it was a Mercedes vehicle and then one could also read, on the equipment found in the vehicle, and the weapons, the name Mustafa Haris Plicanic. And then it goes on to say that the Serb MUP has decided that the -- has discovered that the functionaries of the Muslim and Croatian MUP are organising and preparing terrorist organisations against prominent Serbs, intellectuals and activists, and that they have already organised. Is that something that was established by the police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, go on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case mentioned here, this incident, is something that I'm very familiar with because -- both the first case where the three terrorists were captured, and this other second case, and it was really something that was done by my police, but I don't know how this found its way into the news media because we didn't provide any information. But I recall this very well because we had just begun our work and reorganised the police and we weren't very familiar with the ground, and I know that the situation was under much better control at Ilidza than it was in Hadzici, where I wasn't able to work as effectively. I remember this but I cannot really comment on how this found its way into the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can we scroll up the document a bit and see the name of the journalists, Nedeljko Zugic. He probably received this from a ministry. Yes, we can see that this was received from the Ministry of Information. Does that explain things a bit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is possible because the way we worked at the time was to provide written information to our superiors and the centre, central authorities, but I never did so myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1067, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can it be concluded, then, that up until this time, there are no overt clashes and conflicts up until the 19th of May -- or rather, the 17th of April, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Up until the 17th of April, there was no fighting, no overt clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that the leadership left for Pale as early as the 5th of April, as soon as the conflict in the city itself broke out?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but I do remember that that was in early April, when you left for Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that -- whether Hasan Efendic -- or, rather, that he had issued two directives on the 12th and 14th of April, about an all-out attack against the JNA, the Serb side, and the Serbian Democratic Party, and that following that, there was a small attack or minor attack on Ilidza and then on the 22nd of April, ensued a major attack on Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not really -- I don't know anything about that personally. I just heard of that, but I was not at Ilidza or in Ilidza at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But on the 22nd of April, did you provide assistance to Ilidza because it had come under attack?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, and were you informed, that Ilidza had been attacked, the Serb part of Ilidza, from outside but also from within Ilidza by the Muslims who lived on the Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only was I familiar with this but Mr. Tomislav Kovacevic was in charge of the police and the situation at Ilidza was really alarming, and I remember that at one point, he sent a panicky request for assistance because he said, you know, You come and help us because tomorrow it will be too late. But let me also add that Ilidza and Hadzici are contiguous territories and we always supported each other. I always received support from the police, but also from Mr. Tomislav Kovac or, rather, especially from him, so that we had already had different types of cooperation and that is why we also had received their assistance and they sent some units to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did this affect the general atmosphere and the general state of mind of the Serb population, this attack on Ilidza by the Muslims? In other words, am I correct in saying that the civilian population was terrified but also furious primarily with us because we did not prepare them sufficiently for -- to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What document, Mr. Karadzic, are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we have in e-court, it is a statement about these incidents, the discovery of weapons and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we not marked it for identification already?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When the conflict erupted, what was the situation with your chain of command? Is it correct that the communications were down, the telephones, that they were compromised and damaged?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was especially the case with the public security station in Hadzici, and I've already said in one of my statements that we had to move to an improvised building so that we had no means of communication other than phones. We didn't have the teleprinter, radio communications, no communications whatsoever. All we had was couriers, you know, you write a document down, you write something down, and then you give it to the courier to take it to an address.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 80 of your amalgamated statement, on page 32 and 33, you say that, for example, the political leadership including Karadzic issued instructions for convoys with students leaving Sarajevo, the -- can the participants find this or do I have to call it up in e-court? The convoy has to be allowed to get to Ilidza -- through Ilidza to central Bosnia. [In English] "We had a lot of problems implementing this on the ground. Dr. Karadzic and his associates had a plan that he wanted to effect, but on a later period, there was a different development on the field. I especially mean in the area of Ilidza and Hadzici. I had a feeling that the people in these areas were left to care for themselves. For example, Dr. Karadzic or his political associates never came to Hadzici." [Interpretation] What is described and suggested in this paragraph, that the local authorities during the first months of the conflict were primarily left to their own devices and that there was no communication between local and central authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And just a small addition. When I commented upon that, when speaking to the Prosecution, I wanted to say that it was easy for you and your leadership because you made declarations about certain matters, but that we had terrible problems to implement certain things. So it's along those lines, that it really has to do with what I said already. What you read out now is something that I firmly stand by, that we were left at everyone's mercy down there. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 90221. This is a record from the cantonal court in Sarajevo. Could we have page 27?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is your testimony in the Jovicic case, right? Do you remember that you testified there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the second answer that you gave. Viewed from the top: "Witness, so from the very beginning, how did people transfer from the reserve police to the military police?" And then the witness, you, say: "Well, you know, how can I say, in the territory of the municipality, I mean --" The president of the Chamber says: "Was that according to one's wishes and affinities?" And the witness says: "In the territory of the municipality where I worked, in the area of which I was chief of police, this is how things worked, because we had very poor communications with -- I mean our higher organs, so I mean in that sense, the centre of public security and the ministry itself did certain work at local level, but along with the decisions of the Crisis Staff?" Is that what you confirmed during that testimony as well, namely this absence of communication with higher organs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. It is obvious.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this page be admitted? Or, if it's sufficient to have it in the transcript as I have read it out, we can deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's do that in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now place on the ELMO the proofing notes that we received from you through the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was a few days ago, on the 13th of February, 2011. You spoke to Barry Hogan. Could you please look at the first paragraph? I'm going to read it out in English: [In English] "KDZ589 stated that while the SDS had good organisation before the war, from the republic level to the municipal level, when the war broke out things became chaotic." [Interpretation] Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at the next highlighted paragraph. [In English] "KDZ589 feels that if the SDS had such great organisation, then it would have -- not have been possible that so many Serb people were caught by surprise and detained as they were." [Interpretation] So that was your feeling? Actually, the Serb people were caught by surprise and totally unprepared, right? The pre-war system of communications and the structure was falling apart, and there were no proper solutions that were required by the new developments?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was, but I don't see why you're taking this out of context. Everything I said is contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I can read all of it out but we don't have enough time.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, all right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why don't you provide the context, then? You lived in the Muslim area, there is a reference to Mr. Bratic here and so on. You can tell us quite fairly how all of this happened.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you something. I don't know how this appeared in writing. I spoke to Madam Prosecutor, and I thought that it was a more or less informal conversation, and I wanted to provide my own views regarding this organisation that permeated all of the questions that were put to me from the lowest level to the highest level, organisation in its entirety. I was just trying to explain that things were not functioning, and I tried to demonstrate this by providing a few examples from the municipality of Hadzici. To this day, that is what I claim. I simply cannot accept that someone thinks that there is some kind of proper organisation in place, when there are drastic examples that can tellingly demonstrate that no such concept ever existed, that there was this marvellous communication between the top leadership and us. I see that there is a reference here in English, there is a reference to Bratic, Mile Bratic. At this meeting that was discussed a few moments ago, he was practically elected commander of the Serb Territorial Defence. He lived in an area that was under the command of the Bosniak forces, so practically he was taken prisoner there like all other Serbs. I was trying to explain that, what kind of organisation there was and how all of that functioned. When a commander of the Territorial Defence who had just been elected is staying in an area under Bosniak control and is detained immediately, he was a prisoner at the silo straight away, and unfortunately, I have to say the man is five years younger than I am and he died years ago. How do I explain this entire situation, when it is true that over 500 Serbs in the area of Pazarici, Tarcin and wherever else were taken prisoner. That is what I tried to explain. So you cannot really put it that way. I don't want to take up too much time because I've already said this, I mean how the first and second attack in Hadzici was repelled. This was not organised by the SDS. It is citizens who organised this, a few of them prominent citizens, along with the assistance of the technical institute. The only fortunate thing for the Serb people in Hadzici was that the technical institute was there on that territory and it gave a major contribution to the defence of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I understand it this way, then? Although before the war, the SDS was organised politically, but this political organisation was not accompanied with appropriate preparations for defence and that kind of organisation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I forgot to mention when I spoke to Ms. Carolyn about this. I see that there are two basic distinctions there. What you said just now, I'm not challenging that. The Serb Democratic Party that had an excellent organisation before the war and it had a very good infrastructure from the highest to the lowest level, everything functioned like clockwork, the organisation of the Serb people and so on and so forth, and that went on, including distribution of weapons. However, at the very moment when war operations broke out, and I can say that with certainty, and I imagine that's the way it was everywhere, the organisation was shattered. Local organisations were left to their own devices. People on the ground were left to their own devices. That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED: [Interpretation] Is this sufficient, the fact that we have this in the transcript? Or should we adopt this document as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we need to admit this. It won't be necessary. They are already in the transcript. If I can add, to this, if the witness is to be agreeing with whatever you're going to put, you don't have to put documents before him, necessarily, but it's up to you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us go on and then we are going to see whether we need the document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the very outset, there was no system in place and then a new system had to be created, and this meeting on the 11th of April of the Serb representatives in the municipality of Hadzici was in that context, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the later period, as state authority was slowly being established and laws being passed, were more and more instructions coming in from the central level to your level, the local level?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what period you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 74 of your amalgamated statement, on page 31. I'm going to read it out in English so that you can receive interpretation. [In English] "Directives from military, political and police ministry ordered that these paramilitary forces be subordinated to the military commands and ought to be disbanded and even liquidated if they refused." [Interpretation] Is it correct -- is it correct that such instructions could come only in the later period, from May onwards, May, June, et cetera, because of the disintegration of the system?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't know. My comment had to do with the presence of paramilitaries so that's why I didn't understand. At any rate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After May, after May, so it's not from the beginning of May but from May onwards. From that point of view, were there any instructions that pertained to the protection of civilians of other ethnic backgrounds, then also the honouring of international humanitarian law, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that the second half of 1992 was spent establishing law and order as such?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is quite correct. All public security stations, including my own, the one that I headed, were busy at first with permanent war operations. Later on, we moved on to something that I cannot exactly call peacetime structure, but at any rate, we did go back to our regular work as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to go back to that, the capacity of the police and the number of active duty policemen. I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 62 of your amalgamated statement, page 26. Sorry, actually, do you have your statement in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out in Serbian, then: [In English] "So you were informed by the commander of this action." [Interpretation] It has to do with the action in Musici, the police action. [In English] The answer is: "Yes." "Q. He told you that three persons got killed?" Answer is: "Yes, I found out that the action was taken in Musici hamlet, that's where -- that there was an armed resistance and that these people unfortunately got killed." "Q. Did the crime police officer conduct an investigation as to the deaths of the three civilians or residents and one of the Serbs, as you said? "A. If you are referring to the classic standard crime scene inspection, I don't think that there were conditions in place to carry out a crime scene inspection. But some operative actions and activities were taken and I'm sure that this was -- that the full information was delivered in writing and then forwarded to the centre and to the higher chain of command in the Ministry of Interior." [Interpretation] Are you suggesting by way of this paragraph that the state organs -- actually, can we conclude that state organs were concealing this or other crimes, or did they document them? Actually, were there attempts to hush things up, and after providing documentation, can one speak of hushing up generally?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's out of the question. The main purpose was exactly to present this kind of situations until such time comes that we can undertake certain measures. But as I said, we were not able to carry out standard crime scene investigations due to the prevailing situation. This was only written in documents and then forwarded to the competent institutions such as the centre and the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that even nowadays, both in the federation and Republika Srpska, there are trials based on criminal reports and other documents provided during the war, do you find that convincing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Karadzic, move on to your next topic. I said, how relevant is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to find out whether the police documented certain things and whether that would be forwarded to the courts was up to the circumstances. I all -- wanted to know whether, as a rule, police filed all the crime-related documents.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can tell you with full certainty, not only about this case but about hundreds of other cases, and everything is recorded, everything that happened in Hadzici and Ilidza, that was of security interest. We only had certain gaps and shortcomings in the initial period. However, in the latter part of 1992, until the end of the war, I say categorically that everything was recorded. You, yourself, would be surprised if you saw how many documents exist that are going to be used at the trials in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation. Did it ever happen that somebody intervened from a higher level for certain incidents to be covered up?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such experience, and I don't think that anyone else does, but I particularly didn't have such experience.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we have 3244 -- 1D3244 in e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a document that you produced for the month of April 1992. We don't have a translation but we can see what it means. Does this document prove who was on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We will give you the translation within a couple of seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence would be extremely grateful if we could receive a translation along with the original, but that's going to be rectified at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Glavas, does this document show that on your payroll you had 30 police officers, including the chiefs, commanders, deputy commanders, and you only had 25 regular police officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about April 1992, is it correct, as you said a minute ago, that out of this number, a considerable number of people mentioned here were involved in defence operations rather than in police work?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they nearly didn't do any police work at all. They were very much occupied and busy in war operations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence, since we have the translation so it doesn't have to be marked for identification first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1068, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And we've e-mailed the translation across the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D3245, which refers to the following months? And let's look at the situation then. 1D3245.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the list of employees serving at your station in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I can't see the whole list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please scroll up and after that I'd like to see page 2. Can we move now to page 2, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems that you have been -- had been reinforced during that month by two additional policemen, because we see there are 32 of them now on the list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence? I believe there is a translation of this document as well in the hands of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's also just been e-mailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit D1069.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we now have 1D3246?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were policemen being killed during that period, Mr. Glavas?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the last month of your tenure in Hadzici, i.e., July 1992. Now we see that you had lost seven men in one way or another, and that along with the executive personnel, you have a total of 25 staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As well, we have English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. We will mark it for identification. Or do we need an English translation? Let's do that. Yes. We mark it for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1070, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in addition to these police officers, every police station had some administrative staff, so you are not counting them as members of the police staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that we had these services set up at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3239, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your response to the request from the ministry for information about the structure and the situation in your station. A total number of active duty police officers required for the police station to successfully carry out its duties is 44; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we had some serious thought at that point that the police station should start doing its duties and jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But previously it says that you had 26; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then there is a note which says that we have exhausted all the possibilities of recruiting a larger number of reserve police officers because they were engaged in other units as military conscripts. Can we scroll up so that you can see this part of the document? We note that we have exhausted the possibility of engaging a larger number of reserve police officers because supposedly these reserve police officers are military conscripts and are engaged in other units. Is that the point?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because at that point, since we had so few people, I think that the priority was given to army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were proposing to increase up to 200?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note again there are so many documents untranslated. Having said that, we will mark it for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1071, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that last week we presented around 100 documents and that I think that fewer than five have been translated, but I do accept your criticism and we will do our best to remedy this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You had information about large-scale arrests of Serbs who remained in the areas where Muslims were a majority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like now to remind you of a sequence of certain events, so feel free to tell me, "yes" or "no," or that you don't know. So it's totally up to you. I'm not expecting you to know everything, but as a member of the police force, I suppose you knew a lot. In October of 1991, the SDA's deputies -- SDA deputies acted arrogantly and that prompted the SDS deputies to walk out of the parliament sessions. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, in 1991 and 1992, the Serbian population in Hadzici were restless and anxious, and due to that, they posted guards in the Serbian villages, in fear of being attacked by somebody; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we say that as far as back in March of 1992, reasonable Serbs and Muslims set up joint patrols in order to provide the protection for their villages and create the sense of security?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely true. In the majority of mixed settlements, we had situations of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the 8th of May, the Muslims blocked the entrance to the repair and maintenance centre and that negotiations were initiated, but that during the night, they withdrew after fire was exchanged between Muslim and Serbian villages?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have information here that on the 9th and 10th of May, 1992, the Muslims, at their own initiative, left the centre of the town of Hadzici towards Pazaric and Tarcin. Is that what you refer to as a departure that was carried out according to the Crisis Staff order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it, but I don't think I mentioned that particular date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that about one or two days later, there was a clash between the Muslims and the Serbs because the Serbs -- the Muslims attacked Hadzici from Tinovo and Igman in the early morning hours?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that from the 11th of May onwards, there was daily fire opened at Hadzici from artillery weapons and from sniper rifles and that the whole area was encircled by the Muslims except the route that led to Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but later on, it turned out to be sporadic fire that was an attempt to tie up our forces. Actually, the idea behind that was to attack the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So on the 12th of May, they captured the Krupska Rijeka barracks and killed a number of JNA soldiers in the process and captured a number of them. Until 1993, that was Muslim-run prison for the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in late May 1992, there was a conflict between members of the JNA and the Muslim forces? Thank you. Let us look at a specific example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we hear the answer to the last question? Did you say yes, Mr. Glavas? Because your answer was not translated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that about the attack on the Krupska Rijeka barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go into some detail regarding the Musici incident. Is it true that the JNA was legally in Bosnia-Herzegovina until 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Musici incident take place on the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the Musici incident was preceded by a successful action in Krupska Rijeka and the capture of the barracks there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now shed some light on the situation although you came only after the Musici event. Is it true that people were killed on both sides in Musici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. The first one to be killed was a Serb, I think his name was Zoran Pusara, and after that, three Bosniaks were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there fire opened on a daily basis from Musici on the road leading to Donji Hadzici and was a decision taken to search for weapons in Musici actually prompted by these constant fire?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Musici itself, had Muslims already been organised in military units and had their squads, platoons and so on, in other words military organisation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe I've already mentioned that in the BH court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 65 ter 90221? This is your testimony in Sarajevo, before the Sarajevo court, in the Jovicic case. Page 21, please. We have page 21. Could we please see 24? Here we see the first answer that you gave there. The question was whether the police had noticed before those conflicts that the civilian population was leaving Hadzici, and then your answer: "Well, yes, you see, it was a very special situation down there in Hadzici. At the moment when the police was divided, what followed practically was the division of all the other institutions, government institutions, in the municipality. And what we observed, and that was very indicative and would later have ramifications, was that at this time we observed mass movements of the civilian population out of the municipality. In other words, a large majority of the population was moving from Grivici, for instance, towards Ormanje, from Dupovci towards Pazarici, from Zunovnica towards Igman. There was a mass pullout of the population and we knew that an all-out attack would follow, which, in fact, materialised and happened on the 20th of May, I believe." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. This is what I said in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, no one forced them to leave but, rather, as you said, on orders from their Crisis Staff, they moved out, which led you to conclude that there would be an attack, which is, in fact, how it happened.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did not interpret anything. We knew for a fact that there would be an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As you were not present during the attack in Musici itself, I would move on to another incident.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 65 ter 1549? Your Honour, if you feel that this is sufficient, we need not tender this document into evidence, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's up to you, but speaking for myself, I don't think we need to admit this, given that everything he confirmed is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 1549, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report, it was admitted as D317. It's an exhibit already. And it says, a report of the 28th, I believe, of May 1992. No, 29th of May, 1992. If we look at the last paragraph, it says: "Following the situation, the enemy assess that they could, if they prepare a terrain attack with arms against Zunovnica storage with a force of an infantry battalion. The attack took place on the 25th of May, 1992, in early morning hours, and from two directions. One company along the axis of Crne Stijene-Zunovnica station -- could we move on to the next page in Serbian, please? Thank you. And the 2nd Company should move along the axis Lokve-Kasetici-Zunovnica storage with the purpose of taking over the depot premises. They were largely successful and took control of three-fourths of the storage premises and the buildings there." Is this consistent with what happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can skip the next paragraph, and then, we can read: "After taking in consideration the entire situation, the commander of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Main Staff decided to deploy a strengthened combat group under the command of the chief of the Serb artillery, Colonel Zivanovic." I hope everyone can see this. "And that on the 26th of May, 1992, at 1900 hours, they accomplished that mission and recaptured part of the depot. In the first combat phase, that is, until the combat group arrived, we had the following losses: Dead, 15 soldiers; wounded, 25; and missing, 9; and one defender of Kasetici village was killed; slaughter of members of the Serb population of Kasetici village, six." Were these civilians who were slaughtered?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were criminal complaints and the perpetrators of this crime are -- were discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then it goes on to say, in the second phase, when the combat group arrived, there were no casualties. And then there follows a report on what had been looted from the depot. Now, could you tell us please what these Zunovnica barracks, what was that, whose was it, who it did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zunovnica depot was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat his answer from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, could you repeat your answer? The interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a barracks, or rather, a depot of the former JNA, which housed a number -- a large quantity of ammunition and shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to the number of buildings mentioned here, was -- would you say that this is a large number of facilities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, there were few -- there were many more than here, than mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This village of Kasetici, where the six civilians were slaughtered, was that a Serbian village in Hadzici municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I wouldn't say it was Serb. It was a mixed village. There were both Bosniaks and Muslims, in one part there were Bosniaks, and in another Serbs, and unfortunately the Serbs who were there, they were slaughtered by their neighbours, their Muslim neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now have the next page in Serbian and the English is fine. That's exactly the part we need. "After stabilising our own lines, we -- it is our assessment that we inflicted large losses on the enemy in personnel. According to our information so far, the losses that the enemy suffered were around 130 personnel. Following stabilisation of our own ranks, we approached to the realisation of two main tasks as follows: First, mobilisation of men and establishing of the Hadzici Battalion infantry -- Infantry Battalion. We have difficulties with this task because armed men are self-organised and they have very skewed convictions concerning their defences and the defences of their own homes." Is this consistent with what you could observe at this time at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This was a daily occurrence, and I have to say that we had great difficulty to actually defend our own doorsteps, and chasing people away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have the next page, could we scroll up the English version or, rather, could we have the next page in both versions? In English it's the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something about the work obligation. Is that something that was regulated by law in the former Yugoslavia in wartime conditions? In other words, that all civilians were to be mobilised either in military units or to be engaged in work units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct. That was regulated by the Law on All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see that it is proposed that all able-bodied men in the repair and maintenance centre should cease to be paid employees that apply in peacetime, but, rather, be assigned to work details that would apply in wartime conditions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did this work obligation, is that something that applied to all citizens regardless of their faith or ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now, please, have 65 ter 1648? 65 ter 1648.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that at one point in time, in the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici, at the municipality of Hadzic, a forward unit of the Ministry of Defence was established, which was the case per establishment in each municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this Ministry of Defence section deal with mobilisation and civilian affairs in the service of the army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here we see a report on their work between August 1st and December 20th, 1992. Can we now have the next page, please? Can we have page 3, please? Here we see mention is made of the establishment of this unit pursuant to the Law on the Army and it also cites the law on which -- on the basis of which it was established. And then it says that it shall be responsible for organising and the carrying out mobilisation in work organisations and so on and so forth. Now, let's see item 2 here on this page, the establishment of defence organs, and then it says: "At the request of the Ministry of Defence, on the 16th of July, 1992, a section of the Ministry of Defence of Hadzici was established and Stojic Milovan was appointed as its chief." This was, in other words, at the proposal of the Executive Council that had been established on the 18th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what Executive Council or board you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, in any case, at the proposal of some Executive Council, this person, Milovan Stojic was appointed chief of the office and this occurred on 16th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I am aware of that, and this person, I'm familiar with his name, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say that the situation is as follows: All previous records have been destroyed, part of them were taken to the command of the city of Sarajevo, part were taken -- a part of them were taken by the SDA. And then can we have the next page in Serbian? The reporting centre was practically disestablished, plundered and demolished, all communications equipment stolen. And then it says it was necessary to start from scratch. The circumstances surrounding the establishment of this organ were as follows: All military records have been destroyed, the territory of the former municipality was cut in half. New refugees have already arrived. Is it correct that Hadzici was on the front line, as it were, towards Herzegovina and the areas under the control of the Muslim army, and that a large number of refugees actually came into Hadzici from those areas?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did refugees begin coming already at the time while you were still in Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the municipality had the obligation to accommodate these people and to provide food for them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was our responsibility, of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these people were unhappy and very angry and that it was necessary to take extraordinary effort in order to stop them from taking action to avenge whatever had happened to them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at what it says later on. In this context, this organ was an active participant in taking -- in the context of these activities, this organ participated in the reception of three large convoys of refugees from Zenica, Kakanj, Vitez, and Busovaca. It was necessary to -- can we have the next page, please? The next page in Serbian. It was necessary to receive, accommodate, register, and place these people in different homes. And in addition to these three convoys, there were also numerous smaller groups of refugees arriving. So is this what happened? Did the municipality take action to receive these refugees and did this actually drain the municipal funds?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the greatest problem was, in fact, with these mass exodus from central Bosnia of refugees who then came into Hadzici, and I believe that those refugees were the ones who created the most problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian? I believe that we had it in English, that particular section. I would like to draw your attention to this: "Various orders and letters were used in order to establish communication with the General Staff of the army and the Presidency, but we didn't manage to do that it. In mid-September, we managed to break down this barrier and establish operation, that is at enviable level today." Does this confirm the information that you gave, namely that central organs could not be reached easily before mid-September?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that confirms precisely what I said a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in Serbian? I believe it's the last page in English as well. Now, this is what it says down here, that various certificates and permits within its jurisdiction shall be issued. Is it correct that whoever would want to move about freely would have to seek a certificate stating that he was already engaged in work obligation or in the military?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that useful for that particular person, in order to ensure freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With appropriate papers one could move about, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what it says what the problems here are. Inadequate premises, lack of basic equipment, insufficient cooperation with responsible institutions, strong pressure for engagement on the basis of work obligation. Is it correct that most people wanted to have work obligation, that they preferred it to wartime obligation and that this brought the possibility of getting a bit of a salary and some extra food and so on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. People avoided wartime obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So people, the population, were seeking work obligation. I'm asking you this because sometimes work obligation is termed as negative discrimination. Does this seem to show that that is positive discrimination, when you get work obligation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was positive discrimination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, is it time for the break? Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be Exhibit D1072.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I was informed that the Prosecution has provided us a translation of D1071 and we'd appreciate if that could be admitted as an exhibit rather than MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you confirm that, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done. We will have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We saw what you knew and what your position was, namely that there weren't enough contacts between the local level and the central level, and as a matter of fact, people out there felt betrayed. And I would like to show you paragraph 24 of your consolidated statement, on page 9. I'm going to read it out: [In English] "Politicians at this time did not really count on controlling Hadzici because of the Bosniak majority. A lot of success was attributed to Radic and that's another reason he remained there, but this was really an illusion. Radic spent most of his time with Karadzic in Pale during this critical period." [Interpretation] Can you tell us specifically which critical period you meant? Before the war broke out or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it refers to the period before the war broke out. May I just add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could not have pertained to the period when the war broke out because I remember that in one passage of the statement I gave in Sarajevo, I said that Mr. Ratko Radic for a while - actually, I think I actually referred to the date too - was absent from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that -- sorry, are you referring to the outbreak of war in Sarajevo on 6 April or are you referring to the outbreak of war in Hadzici a bit later?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I said, I was referring to the areas I know very well, Hadzici and Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that before the war broke out, on the 6th of April, I was in Sarajevo throughout and that until the 1st of March, until the barricades were put up, I did my regular work, I went to the clinic to work?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, let us see what the people thought there, that the Serbs were not counting on the municipality of Hadzici because there was not a Serb majority there. Do you remember, I think we mentioned that, that in case the peace were to be maintained, that municipalities would be organised, namely, wherever possible, two municipalities should be established, and in that sense, the Serb municipality had counted on having two municipalities set up in the municipality of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The talks that you referred to in this paragraph have to do with this time before the war, and it's on the assumption that there will be no war, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the next paragraph of your statement, paragraph 25, you say: [In English] "Ratko Radic's relationship, as Crisis Staff president and SDS president, with Radovan Karadzic and the Serbian Republic leadership was very good. I think that he had very good communication with Dr. Karadzic and connections. I base this on his trips to Pale. He would often say that he came from Pale and got instructions from Dr. Karadzic. You could tell from his behaviour that he was close to Dr. Karadzic. I can't give you any concrete examples when he came back with orders, but I can just tell you that he regularly went to Pale to visit Karadzic. He often went to Pale with Vido Banduka, president of the Executive Board of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici. Also Nevenko Samoukovic and Radislav Pejetic [phoen] would travel to Pale with Radic to meet with Dr. Karadzic. They were all presidents of the municipality Executive Board at different times. Ratko Radic always remained in his position of a president of the municipality until the end of conflict." [Interpretation] Do you remember that a moment ago we saw a document stating that it was only in mid-September that this barrier could be broken through, namely that the state leadership could be reached?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you mean the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. Am I right when I say that that was the impression that had been created, that Radic had created, however, you never saw the instructions that Radic received from the state leadership, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly what it's all about. It has to do with impressions. Very often he told us that he was with you up there in Pale and he did this very unpleasant thing. Whenever he wanted to have any idea carried through in that area, he always referred to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you briefly whether you remember that the very existence of the Crisis Staff was a regular thing, when there would be power cuts, when, for example, these days there was no gas coming in from Russia, when there would be an earthquake and things like that, that a Crisis Staff would be established?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, practically every time something like that happened, a Crisis Staff would be established, before the war as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that Crisis Staffs, or, rather, War Presidencies, or, rather, these smaller organs of government were actually supposed to stand in for larger organs like parliament when parliament could not meet, like in war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that all decisions of the state leadership and of the municipal leaderships were supposed to be confirmed at the sessions of parliament that would be held as soon as possible, both at state level and at municipal level?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at 65 ter 1523? Can we go back to the critical events that were taking place in the municipality itself? Of course, we are going to deal with this through documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have to go back to the 12th of May. Please focus on all of it. But we have this second paragraph here, sorry, can we agree that this was on the 12th of May, 1992, and that is the Ministry of the Interior? This is a bulletin of daily events, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what the police is reporting about what happened on the 12th of May, the second paragraph: "Heavy exchange of fire between Serb defence forces and members of the TAR," I guess that's Tarcin Territorial Defence -- oh, TZV, that is so-called, the so-called TO of the former BiH has been going on for more than two days in the Hadzici area. "Despite the unequal balance of forces with Serbs being fewer in numbers, attacks of Muslim paramilitary formations have been resisted successfully. The situation in Hadzici is still very difficult, at the moment, the area of Krupacka Rijeka, Tinovo Brdo and JNA facilities in Zunovnica are besieged. However, Serb forces control this area and have the situation under control for the time being." Does this have something to do with that attack of the Green Berets that is referred to in that previous sentence up there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what was meant here was the attack that took place against the barracks in Krupa. Now, the sporadic gunfire around Hadzici, as I said a few moments ago, this was manoeuvring on their part to draw our forces away so that they could carry out an attack, as they did at the barracks in Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to shed more light on the question of paramilitaries and their relations with the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this previous document be admitted, this daily bulletin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1073, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we have 1D3240, which is identical to 65 ter 23088, and I think it would be more advisable if we call up 23088. On the 6th of August, you left Hadzici. Do you remember leaving behind of certain aggregate report concerning the events that happened up until that time? So that was sent, or, rather, dated 9th of, August, 1992, it was sent to the Sarajevo CSB, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I remember is based on the comments given by the OTP. I am more or less familiar with the content, and as far as I can recall, I can see that my name is there and my signature is there, but it was not me who signed it. Although there is mention of certain things that pertained to my period, by that time I was already in Ilidza. It is dated the 9th, and I was at Ilidza already at the 6th. Practically, I hadn't been relieved of my duty of the police chief in Hadzici, so apparently somebody signed this on my behalf. However, if you want to ask me about the contents of this document, I don't see any problem because I am more or less familiar with those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is a case relating to a 1993 document which is close to the period while you were between two positions, but am I to understand that the contents of this document is consistent with the knowledge that you have, because three days prior to this date, you were in charge of that centre?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with all the events described in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I now direct your attention to item A? I'm not going to read it all. And here you explain that after the setting up of the Serbian police station Hadzici, or in the process of its forming, and in the following 14 days, we noticed the activities of certain small groups of so-called 'free agents,' but there were no significant or proper paramilitary units in that period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And you have here "free agents" in inverted commas. That's how we called those young guys who had weapons and who thought that they had free hand. They didn't want to put themselves under anyone's control or to become part of any formation, and that is why we called them as we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you said that immediately thereafter, you proceeded with providing the protection -- I'm a little bit in a hurry. It was not recorded that you said that you had problems with them because they had weapons and they didn't want to place themselves under the control of either military or the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. We had a lot of problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you go on to say in this same paragraph that: "In the period while the police station was being formed and in the initial period, we started most seriously dealing with carrying out primarily providing the protection of citizens and their safety and property, in securing public law and order, and detecting criminal offences and perpetrators thereof." When you say "citizens," did you refer to any citizen regardless of their ethnicity or faith?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your own family, do you have people who are of different ethnic or religious affiliation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My wife is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the next page? I believe we have to move to the next page in English as well. Now, you say that until that moment there had been no paramilitary formations. However, there is indications of insertion of small groups [indiscernible] sabotage and terrorist groups. And then you go on to say, as mentioned above, small groups and individuals, so-called free agents, committed crimes of theft from other persons, mainly of movable property and assets, thus gaining unlawful material gain for themselves or others. A certain small number of military conscripts and members of the police station did not stay immune to such activities. One has to underline here that an organisation, the greater part of illegally acquired property, mainly vehicles, was seized from police officers and placed at certain locations and that measures are being taken to seize vehicles and other illegally acquired property from other citizens. And then it says in the period from April to July, police officers of this police station were engaged in all combat activities which was necessary at the time, and since 1st of August, 1992, a large number of police officers returned from the front lines and were placed back on regular MUP activities, as can be seen in the following table per month. So during this period, while they were on the front line, they were unable to carry out their regular police work, nor was anyone able to do that instead of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also highlighted here the need to purge the police force because it had been noted that some of the police officers were involved in committing crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely so. I believe that I made a comment to the OTP also to the effect that during this period of war operations at the beginning of war, we were considerably weakened because we applied very bad criteria when recruiting members of the police, which opened up the door for people prone to crime to enter our ranks. Therefore, we had to purge our own force because we knew, unless we do that, we would never be able to carry out the work that we were expected to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we see that in April, there were 105 combat activities in which police took part, which meant more than three a day on the average. In May there was 130, more than four a day, and these figures dropped slightly in June and July, and we have regular activities in three and five cases, respectively; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
