utterances.text: Yes. I think this is consistent with what I said yesterday in examination-in-chief, which is to say that in addition to combat activities, starting from June, more or less, we started carrying out security service work as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now move to the next page, please? I'm not going to read everything. I would just like all the participants to look at sub-item C, we have it in the Serbian as well, and it describes what was being done. The detection of perpetrators, an increase the number of criminal offences, theft, aggravated theft, theft of motor vehicles, unauthorised entry into apartments and other rooms, an increasing number of perpetrators of criminal offences -- of perpetrators of criminal offences in addition to the known or unknown perpetrators from the area of Hadzici municipality, including a large number of perpetrators from the areas of other municipalities, as well as perpetrators of criminal offences who are in the municipality as refugees from the area of Zenica and other places; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the emergence of these identified perpetrators and the large number of refugees meant deterioration of the conditions of your work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later detection of crimes and perpetrators was something that was done by a small number of members of the police stations. Can we now move to the next page in both versions, please? The station is lacking in most basic equipment and forensic equipment, such as sufficient number of communications systems, et cetera, et cetera. And it also says that they are involved in large number of combat operations. Can we move to the next page now, please, because we are going to tender this document. I'm not going to read all of it. Now I need page 5. It says here: "As regards providing and exchanging information --" can you confirm or deny in your mind, is there a difference between a prisoner or a detainee -- a prisoner of war and/or a detainee?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So when you talk about prisoners, that implies an armed conflict; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the case, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But when we say "detainees," we are talking about perpetrators of crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid that when we talk about prisoners, this refers to the Muslims that were held in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now you say that some of them were moved to the state prison in Kula or released. A smaller number of them are in Hadzici and they are being treated in a fair manner and according to the law. Now, did this state prison in Kula constitute actually a remand prison that existed a long time before the war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In examination-in-chief, Ms. Edgerton showed us the photographs of the municipal building and the garages. Her question contained a statement to the effect that those were the places where the detained Muslims were held. Was the criteria for their detention, their religious affiliation, or was it based on a possible act that they had committed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were mainly Bosniaks, as I said, from Binjezevo, Zunovci [phoen] and Kucice, and most of them were in possession of long-barrelled weapons. They were brought in and interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Some of them were transferred to the state prison in Kula but some were released; is that correct? This is what it says under paragraph D.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have no reason to doubt the veracity of this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here, under E, that there are no military judiciary organised in the area of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, there were no such organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1074, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we have tackled the issue of taking prisoners and capturing, can we now look at 65 ter 10730? And we'll revert to the issue of paramilitary in order to clarify it further. This is a report on the work of the Municipal Committee for the Exchange of Prisoners during the period from, I think the 1st of October until the 21st December, 1992, and certain individuals are mentioned here from both sides who were exchanged. Now, can you please focus on what it says here? And I quote: "Since it was obvious --" it is possible that we are going to be faced again with a bad translation. I'm going to read this and I want the interpreters to interpret this: "Since it was obvious that the previous records were disorderly and unclear, a census of the entire Serbian population in the areas of Tarcin and Pazarici was carried out, as well as of the Muslim population in the Hadzici area under control of the Serbian authorities ..." What it means is that the areas of Tarcin and Pazarici, as it says here, were under Serb control. The translation is not good. So let me continue: "... the Muslim population in the Hadzici area under the control of the Serbian authority, and more precise and clear records of prisoners including the civilians who are free to move around have been established." So in the area of Hadzici municipality, which was under the control of the Serbian forces, there were Muslim civilians who were completely free to move around, on the one hand, and there were Muslims imprisoned on whatever basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat what he says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Records were made of the Serbs who remained in the Muslim-controlled territory; whereas in the territory under Serb control, we have records of the civilians who are free to move around and records of the Muslims who were imprisoned on whatever basis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I think that this primarily refers to the men who were brought to the sports centre, and this term "free citizens" referred to women and children who remained either in Hadzici or in Binjezevo or other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they were Muslim. Now, were there any Muslims of military age who refused and did not actually heed the call-up that was sent out to them, the call-up papers?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no such instances but there were some who did report for work duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They reported for work duty or obligation to the Serbian authorities, correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would now like to tender this document but we would also like it to be translated properly, because the translation actually affects or alters the understanding of the text and the meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, the Muslims who did report for their work detail, were they treated and did they have the same benefits that the Serbs who were under work obligation enjoyed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my view, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned that some actions were taken pursuant to orders from the Crisis Staff. Did it ever occur that the Crisis Staff or any other organ of authority, either police or military, issued orders or allowed or tolerated illegal treatment of detainees?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, there were no such instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this document. However, we would like to have the translation revised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have heard the explanation of the witness, but we'll see how it can be done. We will admit it as Exhibit D1075.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 11574, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will now return to the issue of paramilitary units. Before that, Mr. Glavas, let me ask you this: The document we saw a little earlier, the previous document, which gave a very clear picture of all the abuses, even the abuses that were committed by police officers, so it was very candid -- let me ask you this: Were you as a police officer, the chief, ever asked to actually engage in cover-up?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Nor would that have been permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now we have this document before us. We see that it comes from the Ministry of the Interior, the administration -- the police administration, the Sarajevo police administration. It is sent to the Ministry of the Interior, and it is a report on the realisation of orders, strictly confidential number 10, so on and so forth, of the 27th of July, 1992. And it says: "Pursuant to your order and in accordance with a working agreement with the Romanija Birac CSB chief, I visited most public security stations in that area," and then it goes on to describe where all he had gone. Now can we have the next page? And we see from the top -- and could we have the English page too, the next page. I would especially like to point out that the regrouping and returning or reverting of the tasks from the domain of the organs of Interior are to the public security station, does that mean that they were returning from the front line, that the police officers were returning from the front line? We were waiting for the translation but your answer was yes, obviously. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say, that in most public security stations, the work was analysed and a certain number of staff members whose professional knowledge and moral code is not compatible with the work in the service or who manifested a tendency towards committing crimes during the war, were eliminated from the service. And this task will remain as a permanent one for the next period, and its realisation will be continually monitored. So is it correct that as soon as they again began doing their basic work, the police work, they began a purge in their ranks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now there is -- we next see that they speak of paramilitary units. A special problem in certain areas are paramilitary formations, groups and individuals who waged their own personal wars. True, as I was informed, they respond to and provide support units of the Serbian army and police but obviously they have some special motives for war and so on and so forth. Do you agree that there is a significant -- a major difference between volunteers and paramilitary units? Now, to refresh your memory, do you remember that before the war broke out in Yugoslavia, the Presidency issued a decision regulating the question of volunteers who had to be put under military control?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, true volunteers, actually, who did arrive, they placed themselves under military command, but as for paramilitary units, they were -- they presented a major problem and they were paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A little further down it says in some areas such as in Ilidza and Pale, for instance, they stay in special buildings and are often on the move in different areas. And then on the route Sarajevo-Zvornik, in the course of leaving the field, they leave in groups and create problems for the local public security station, ignoring them or even threatening to attack police officers at the check-point. So would you agree with me that they were a major threat to the police and state organs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think that this document does not stress sufficiently how dangerous they were. It says that they were threatening, but they actually used their weapons and were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, have a clash with one such group while you were in Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, and I believe I said so in my statement to the Prosecution. I don't know if there is a need for me to repeat it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us just briefly what kind of incident this was and whether you were there, whether you were involved in that as a representative of the government?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this happened in May. I was on my way to -- or actually, I attended one of the meetings that we had Ilidza organised by Mr. Kovac, and when I returned to our headquarters, where the police station was housed at the time, and I believe I showed that on the photo, the garages and the ground floor, we had some individuals of Bosnian nationality who were held there. When I arrived at the station, I was told that paramilitary units, and my police officers told me that they were White Eagles or something like that, that they were unfortunately already on the premises of the sports centre and that they mistreated and abused the prisoners in all sorts of ways, and I've also testified about this at the BH court. And when I arrived from Ilidza, they were already in the garages, and because there were other five -- there were some five other police officers, who were reliable police officers, we went there together and asked them, What are you doing here? And they said, Well, we wanted to take these prisoners out and mistreat them. And I said, No, you won't do that. I won't allow it. And then it escalated, our verbal conflict escalated, and then I drew out my weapon, they drew out their weapons, and then my police officers, when they saw me pulling out my weapon, they also pulled out their weapons, and there it kind of ended, and these paramilitary members left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But they outnumbered you, right? There were only five of you, correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. At that point in time I was pretty certain that if we really had an armed conflict, that there were other police officers at the police station who would support us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it say here in this document that their presence in MUP ranks is unacceptable for several reasons? And then it goes on to speak about their duty to be resubordinated either to the police or to the military, but here in this document it says that the police did not want them and that they were unacceptable for various reasons?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, absolutely. There was never a single member of any paramilitary unit within any of the units that I was a commander of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, then, we have a description here of some Chetniks from the detachment Dusan Silni, who were staying in the orchard of Rakovica. They were pretty well organised and independent in their work. Well, this is a reference to Ilidza, in fact. But on the next page we see a reference made to Hadzici. That's on page 3. I don't want to ask you about the period prior to August in Ilidza. Can we have the next page in both versions, please? Can we have the next page in Serbian, page 3? And in English as well. Here we see, in the area of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici, there are some 10.000 inhabitants, there are 26 active and 30 reserve police officers, there are no organised paramilitary formations -- units there, and the situation in the police force is good. These 26 regular police officers, active duty police officers, was that an insufficient number of police officers to deal with these paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously, it was, because there were not many members of paramilitary units there. That's what it says there. There are no organised paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document and then we'll move on to some other municipalities, but I only wanted to ask you about this relating to Hadzici municipality up until the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1076.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 1606, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a similar type of inspection in the field of the 10th of August, and then there is a report. This is an inspection of the Romanija Birac CSB Security Services Centre, do you agree that that's what it says here in the subtitle?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it says relating to -- in relation with the realisation of your order of the 27th of July, 1992. Now let's take a look at the third paragraph, that, together with the chief of the CSB police duties and tasks department, Drago Borovcanin, I perform an inspection of the region of the Ilidza SJB, Vogosca SJB, Centar SJB, and then the public security stations from Pale to Zvornik. But you were in Ilidza at the time already; correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was the deputy chief of the public security station, not the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the last paragraph it says, it was concluded that some substantive changes occurred, when compared to the previous period, because the paramilitary formations were made to leave this area, however not entirely, because some of them still remained in the Vocnjak building, but according to the police station commander and the commander of the Ilidza brigade, this job can be considered to have been completed. Can we now have the next page, please? In Serbian as well, please. This work can be considered done. And then below it says: "I stress that the level of cooperation with the army in the Serbian-held areas is improving and that this area is under constant enemy attacks, and that in terms of material and technical supplies and assets available to the station, this is something that should be especially in focus." And then it goes on to say, while inspecting the region of Vogosca Public Security Station at the work meeting with the chief of the SJB, it says that there was an increase in all types and forms of crime, poor organisation and technical equipment, uncontrolled deployment in the region of a group and so on. So a week later, the same commission revisited the area in order to see what had been implemented. Now, Mr. Glavas, in view of the fact that it was wartime, can it be considered that the commission coming back a week later could actually establish that most of the tasks had been accomplished, correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit D1077.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that it has been admitted already. Can we have the exhibit number, then?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Well, we are still on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at this other part? It says a group of Chetniks that was in this area after Radic's death. This has to do with Boro Radic not Ratko Radic, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After Radic's death they left the area, right? And then it is obvious that in this municipality, 1 per cent of the population are Muslims and Croats. Does that mean a certain percentage not 1 percentage point? Would that be in the spirit of our language?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain percentage, there are some, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So crimes are primarily directed against their property. In talks with the SJB chief and the police station commander, we came upon a conclusion -- we came to the conclusion that there is no inclination and, according to their evaluation, no conditions to prevent the mentioned group in an organised manner, because that would worsen the relations between the Serb population and invoke hostility of the population towards the police because the persons in question are local persons that are known from before as having been prone to crime. Is this something that happened often? Did the police have problems with the population that was exerting pressure to the effect that people who could possibly take part in combat should not be touched?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had problems like that. What you read out now in relation to Vogosca is something that I know personally because at that time I was already in Ilidza, and at Ilidza we had a highly organised and capable so-called special unit. I remember that at that time I sent this special unit there precisely because of these problems. I think I sent them there for some 10 or 15 days precisely to deal with the situation there in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it was easier for you to resolve this with policemen who were not from Vogosca rather than those who were and who were therefore under pressure of the local population?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That primarily meant these young men from the special unit. If necessary, if they were supposed to resort to weapons. They were capable of doing that, too. That's why we sent them inter alia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 18354? That would be the 65 ter number. I can just hope that the audio material will be used for this transcript to be made complete because you and I are not actually making any pauses. This is already the month of September. The Ministry of the Interior, the CSB of Romanija and Birac, to the Public Security Stations Ilidza, Hadzici, Vogosca, all of those that are mentioned here, right? And it says, reference, your documents of the 27th and 28th of July, 1992. It says here that through these documents of ours, you've been made aware of the order of the Minister of the Interior that pertains to activities and measures of urgently dismissing from the Ministry of the Interior employees who -- against whom criminal proceedings have been instituted ex officio, except for political and verbal offences, as well as employees who committed crimes during the war and, for well-known reasons, criminal proceedings were not instituted against them. This is a 65 ter document. Do we have a translation by any chance? It would be easier for the interpreters, too, because I'm reading so fast. Could the Trial Chamber ask Madam? No?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No. And maybe Dr. Karadzic could assist us by slowing down his pace a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was mistaken. That comment was made by the interpreters. Slow down, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this paragraph refer to orders of the ministry to cleanse the police of those who were held criminally liable and those who were not actually charged for well-known reasons because they were still at the front line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then further on, it says -- we are going to skip one paragraph, it says: "In spite of the mentioned obligations, a number of SJBs did not take this subject matter seriously enough. It is the heads of these SJBs that are responsible for that, who are in charge of the SJBs concerned, and who are authorised to do so by way of certain regulations. In order to objectively view this subject matter and inform the Ministry of the Interior about that, and that is what the Ministry is asking us to do, it is necessary for the SJBs that have not done so yet carry out an analysis of possible involvement of employees in the commission of crimes and other violations of work duties as stipulated in the Law on the Interior." This is already the first half of September. Are these measures aimed at introducing rule of law and respect for laws and are we starting with the police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Inter alia, legal regulations are referred to here. So you see, at the time when the war started, it seemed to be different measures were taken by the ministry all the time, actually, because disciplinary proceedings were undertaken within the ranks of the members of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The last two paragraphs: "Public security stations who do not have such cases are duty-bound to confirm that in writing. Likewise, this centre of security services should be notified of such issues including measures taken in the period from the 1st of April, 1992, until the present day. Head of the CSB, Zoran Cvijetic." Were you aware of this action taken by him and it goes all the way down to the chiefs of the public security stations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of it and you saw what it said. It was sent to all the stations, and I remember that it was somewhat different then. I remember that this area went all the way to Zvornik, the organisation was somewhat different at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted -- or, rather, marked for identification until it's translated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1077, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have in e-court 65 ter 18499? It seems that we have a translation, too. That's going to be fine, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the 23rd of November, 1992. It's the same chief of the CSB, Zoran Cvijetic, and Simo Tusevljak is signing on his behalf. It's being sent to the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and it has to do with problems concerning members of the Ilidza Serbian Public Security Station, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just one small correction, it says here that Mr. Zoran Cvijetic, chief of the CSB, received this document from the centre and he practically forwarded it in its entirety to the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He just forwarded it. I see. Right. Already then -- actually, was it in 1993 when you assumed different duties or were you in a different position already then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, by then I had already become centre -- become head of the station in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this is what this document says. On the 14th of November, 1992, at the Kobiljaca check-point, a convoy was stopped and checked by policemen and operatives of the crime prevention service, and then this was interrupted by Brne's Chetniks and the Serbian Guard who entered the buses without asking, and mistreated not only the passengers but also the policemen, belittling their work and drawing firearms at them. Did that happen as described here?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is certainly what happened. We had lots of situations like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on it says, despite being warned about their actions by the chief of the public security station -- that's you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These formations again acted in the same way on the 15th of November in 1992, during a check at the Blazuj intersection, during a check of a convoy with Jewish citizens, where those people tried to enter the buses in an even rougher manner and seized passenger vehicles from the convoy. Energetic action by the policemen prevented these formations from achieving these aims. On the 16th of November, so that's three days in a row, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of November, 1992, a preannounced convoy of Croats and Muslims was stopped in Ilidza with a view to checking them. Policemen and members of the special units secured the convoy and prevented the Chetniks and Serbian Guard who had gathered around the convoy, in spite of warnings not to interfere in the work of the police, from achieving the above-mentioned aims. Please take action in line with the above document and place the said formations under control so that similar situations do not arise in the future and inform us about what has been done citing the above number. So this is the police asking the military to do something about this, to prevent these patriots, who are introducing themselves as members of the armed force but, in actual fact, they are renegades and they are out of control, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. However, the main reason why we sent this kind of a document to the corps was that there is a reference to the Serbian Guard here. You see that? This is a regular part of the Ilidza brigade who sort of got out of control. They were involved in various things that they were not supposed to be involved in, and that is why this kind of document was sent to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you something now that I'm sure that you know. Am I right if I say that when the system changed, certain elements or renegades who were out of control represented themselves as anti-communists, and in that way, they were against regular policemen, regular officers, and this was just intended to mask their irregular behaviour, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1078, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at P2304 for a moment? P2304. Yes, it's a Prosecution exhibit so there is a translation too. This is already the 9th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it's sent to the undersecretary of the National Security Service, Dragan Kijac, and it is the Ministry of the Interior, the Sarajevo CSB that is writing to him, the National Security Service sector. Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. And I know of this document because it was presented to me by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. You see here what it says, that parts of this group appeared there as part of a wedding procession and they were clashing with the military police, and military policemen even had a concussion, pistols were taken away and so on. So, does this mean that there are still clashes going on of this nature even in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to indicate another thing here, namely the difference between volunteers and paramilitaries. Vasilije Vidovic, Vaske, is mentioned every now and then. This paragraph says that he took part in resolving the matter, that he was under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska although he dressed in a rather unconventional way, like American Scouts. Is it true that he belongs to that category of volunteers who accept discipline and obey orders, whereas these who appear as a wedding party are actually paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I know that Chetnik Vaske personally. And I know that he had exceptionally good relations with the then commander of the Ilijas Brigade, and I know that he placed himself under the command of the Ilijas Brigade absolutely and voluntarily and he did not avoid cooperation with the military as opposed to others, including those mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has already been admitted. Now I'd like to ask you whether you remember that you came to Ilidza's aid when it was attacked on the 22nd of April, 1992, and when they were requesting assistance? Hadzici. The Hadzici police came to their aid.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I think that I've already spoken about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. But I wanted to ask you whether you remember how many fatalities there were on the Serb side during that attack of the Muslim Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that Serb Ilidza, the Serb part of Ilidza, was attacked from Sokolovic, Kolonija, Otes, and Hrasnica by the Muslim Green Berets as well as by local Muslims who lived together with Serbs and who shot them in the back?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Should I provide a more extensive explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you whether you know how many people got killed then on the Serb side, approximately.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think it was 15 or 20 victims. I don't know exactly, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this a dramatic turning point in people's minds and was it on that account that Mr. Kezunovic, president of the municipality, resigned?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was one of the reasons. After that attack at Ilidza, especially after realising how people had lost their lives, I mean the situation in Ilidza was truly chaotic. There was fighting in the area that you referred to, and as fighters tried to avoid getting wounded from the other side, they were shot in the back. Later on, it turned out that, regrettably, citizens of Bosniak ethnicity entered the rehabilitation institute and, regrettably, they were wearing medical uniforms. They prepared weapons and when the attack took place, the locals of Ilidza sustained more casualties at the hands of the locals than those who were attacking from the outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, can you tell us when it happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That happened on the 22nd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did this crisis give rise to mutual blaming and the search for those who were responsible for such a situation in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was the main reason for such chaos in Ilidza. I know that my colleague, Kovac, had tremendous problems as a result of this situation. He was even branded as a traitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you refresh our memory briefly about who Predrag Ceranic was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Predrag Ceranic was an ex-operative of the State Security Service of Ilidza. I think that in mid-1992, he took the position of the chief of the public security station in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please now have 1D3243? Let us look now how the National Security Service is reporting about all these accusations, rumours and other allegations. 1D3243. What we see here, is that a National Security Service report from Ilidza dated 25th of June, 1992? Can we please look at the bottom of the page and then -- so it's the 25th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page, please. This won't take too much time because we don't have a translation. And there is your name mentioned, among others who are accusing each other, and it says, the National Security Service has certain indication which are being checked relating to activities and behaviour of security interests in the area of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici. In other words, there is almost total mistrust in this territory, the citizens are expressing their mistrust more and more towards certain important institutions such as the public security station, the army and certain individuals. So at a time of crisis, when solutions are not being found, the people exert pressure on their own institutions. Is this what this is about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's it. I don't find this unusual at all. I had seen much worse situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now there is allegations at your expense and it says that the chief of the SJB of Hadzici, Glavas Tihi, and police station commander Branislav Mijatovic are thought to be very unreliable and there are reports of their cooperating with the opposing side. Now, among the people who are living in fear, was it a practice that any contact with another side was declared treason?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the case, and that was in the period while I was there, although I think that was due to the fact that I try in every possible way to save my father and my two brothers. But I wouldn't want to comment on this any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now move to the next page, but please bear in mind that I'm not taking what is written here at face value. I just want to illustrate the situation. Now, the paragraph 4, it says there is mistrust in the highest government organs in the municipality. So that as soon as there is gunfire, the people from the government flee to Pale, allegedly under the excuse that they were going to talks with the government of the Republic of Srpska. He's talking about rumours and there were such rumours?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please? And he is making his assessments here at the end, by saying although we would not like to make any suggestions, we would like to underline the certain unit commanders of the Serbian army in Hadzici estimate that for -- to ensure a full and successful defence of the Serbian positions, another 100 combatants approximately need to be recruited, and it's signed by Predrag Ceranic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification, pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1079, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 1556?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it, do you agree, nevertheless, that the state leadership thought that these rumours cannot be taken seriously into account and that you did not lose any of your credibility in the eyes of the minister and other state organs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely right. To be honest with you, I didn't know about this report at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, what kind of secret service would that have been, had you known about it? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I have my own opinion about them but this is not the time nor the place to express it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, this is Ilidza, the 4th of June, now, let's see how the foundation was created for these rumours to be spread, but let us also look at the reality of the clashes with the paramilitary formations. Can we have the next page in both versions, please? This is the same author, only now his assessment is that he says that individuals are presenting numerous disinformation about Serbian public security station in Ilidza and about the Ilidza Brigade, with the aim of dividing and sowing mistrust among combatants and citizens in these institutions. This information is entitled "A Rift," so let's look at that. It says here that, according to the information that we have, that when you arrived at Ilidza, you established contact with President Prstojevic which was followed by good cooperation and that you heard that the municipal authorities were blamed for the difficult situation in Ilidza; is that correct? It's not in this document. I'm just giving you a kind of introduction before we get to this document. Do you remember that when you came there, you were introduced to him and you had good cooperation and you didn't have any problems with the municipal authorities in Ilidza despite all these rumours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct. But I don't see any connection with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that because the author is the same. Some of your colleagues suspected that the municipal authorities were tolerating the presence of renegade groups, but did you, yourself, see that they were more afraid, I mean the authorities, of them rather than tolerating them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were situations of that kind in which representatives of the military made such comments to the effect that almost the political authorities were behind such formations, and I can confirm for both municipalities that that was not the case. I know that, particularly in Ilidza, I had an extremely good cooperation and I know what Mr. Prstojevic was doing at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you look at the last two paragraphs on this page, which says that, certain individuals are trying to portray the robberies committed by crimes and certain members of the Serbian TO and some other according to the Crisis Staff order and also the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please slow down and tell us which particular paragraph he is reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters were not able to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm going to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So those who were blamed for the death of members of the Serbian armed forces on the 21st of April, during the first attack on the territory of Serbian Municipality of Ilidza, they accuse the head of the Serbian Public Security Station Ilidza, Tomislav Kovac, despite the fact that the cause of the death can -- can we move now to the next page in Serbian, the English is all right. The cause of their death was a cunning attack by the enemy and poor organisation of the Serbian TO at the time. Do you recall that this is consistent with the process of looking for the -- those who are to be blamed for the loss of these two men in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's it, but I really find it ridiculous to accuse Mr. Tomislav Kovac who, at the time, was by far the most competent man. So it is really pointless to comment on that any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would gladly show you some of the intercepts between Tomislav Kovac and Nedjeljko Prstojevic relating to these events, but I'm afraid that you don't know anything about these intercepts and that you wouldn't be in a position to comment on them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would prefer not to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now skip one paragraph and then it reads as follows: In addition, citizens complained to the Serbian public security station of Ilidza, reporting thefts and forceful expelling of Muslim citizens from Ilidza, committed by "Seselj's men," in inverted commas, However, when the Serbian Public Security Station Ilidza decided that in such cases interventions were necessary, the president of the former Crisis Staff of Ilidza, Nedeljko Prstojevic and his deputy, Radislav Unkovic opposed this decision, stressing out that with Seselj's men there should be no messing around; in other words, that they were doing it on their behalf, since Prstojevic and Unkovic tasked them with it. Is this true or is this just part of this exchange of allegations and accusations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: I'm not familiar with any of this, and I would not like to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Prstojevic and Unkovic were the ones who ordered this or do you think this is just allegations without any foundation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you want my honest opinion, I think that this whole information is suspicious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the term "Seselj's men," in inverted commas. In your view, were White Eagles -- Dusan Silni, were they Seselj's men, were they considered to be Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't consider them as Seselj's men. However, they were members of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because both these formations belonged to other parties but it was commonplace to say that everyone who was not part of the military was a Seselj's man. Now, can we look at the last page, please? I believe that we need the last page in English as well, the last two paragraphs. Before the break let me just finish this. And it says here that Sinisa Milic persuaded Seselj's men to attack and take over the SSJB Ilidza and he succeeded, but they gave up their plan soon realising that energetic retaliation would follow. In regard to this, "Seselj's men," again in inverted commas, behaved in a strange way. Tonight, on the 4th of June, they arrived at the building of the public security station of Ilidza with the intention to take one of the prisoners out, without having obtained the approval of the officer in charge. Once they were not allowed to do that, they, headed by Sinisa Milica, aka Mongo, threatened with weapons until they got the two prisoners from the health centre given to them. On that occasion, Mongo threatened to blast the health centre if their request was not met. The "Seselj's men," in inverted commas, gathered in front of the station under arms and they went away only after they had been warned by the commander of the station and employees of the police. Were you aware of such so-called internal danger that lured from these renegades and could these renegades be considered to be locals?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is mention here of Sinisa Milic, Mongo. I knew that man from Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were these young men prone to committing crimes before?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we admit this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1080, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will have a break, Mr. Karadzic, after which you will have 40 minutes to conclude your cross-examination. We will resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, I would need a few minutes more. I am counting on your standard practice because we are not wasting time really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please try to conclude in that period of time. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have 1658 from the 65 ter list, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are still on the topic of paramilitary units. I'm not going to read out the whole thing but I would like to refer you to the first part, where it says that paramilitary units knew the exact date when the new commander of the Igman Brigade would arrive and they even prepared to assassinate him. And then it says, when the new commander arrived, Colonel Spasoje Cajic, Brne's formation felt that it would not have the privileges that it had had until that time and that it would have to place itself under the brigade command as an integral part of the Republika Srpska army. Upon the arrival of the new commander, Brne came in person to him and told him that he knew everything about him, including the exact time he was to take over the brigade, and one of the Chetniks had told him that he had been in charge of his assassination. Does this reflect the relationship or the attitude of these renegades and what their attitude was to the institutions, official institutions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, but I see also that mention is made here of Velimir Dunjic, he's the previous commander, and also here there should be a correction, this is Spasoje Cojic, not Cajic, there should be an O. And I have to say that he was a little bit prepared to give them freer hand and that he, himself, was in some kind of collusion with these paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on it says further, bearing in mind that the leadership of Republika Srpska had declared that all paramilitary units had to be placed under the joint command of the VRS, we can conclude that it would not be easy or painless to deal with Brne's men. In relation to that, we have to stress that this group of men denigrates and underestimates the Chief of Staff of the VRS, as well as corps commanders and other officers. For them, they claim that they are traitors and Tito's generals, that they are incompetent, while at the same time giving preference to some of their men and units. Thus, for instance, according to Brne, the former JNA officers are a group of incompetents, and Arkan, Captain Dragan and he, himself, were the real fighting force. Is this, in fact, a smokescreen which people like to use, claiming that someone was Tito's general because they were communists?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is typical of their conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see that interpreters are having a difficult time. There should be Tito's generals and communists there. Further on it says, so we have -- it has to be emphasised that they are also bothered by civilian authorities as well as MUP workers, about whom they tell falsehoods and slander them, saying they are thieves, criminals and so on and so forth. Based on this official note from the state security, can we conclude that the civilian authorities were also targeted by these men and that, in fact, they did not enjoy their support and that they were trying to discredit the legal authorities, government bodies?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's correct. It is absolutely out of the question that the government authorities supported them. Perhaps they feared them, but that they supported them, that's out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is an exhibit already. It was signed by Srdjan Sehovac. You do know this officer of state security, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He used to work there and we worked together. We were co-workers at Ilidza Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was one of the Prosecution exhibits that we admitted, P2305.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3241, please? Can we pull it up in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the government authorities actually feared these groups and they tried to avoid getting into conflict with them. Does that mean that the authorities did not have at their disposal a sufficient or strong enough police force in order to be able to deal with them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that was the only problem. We had a large police force in Ilidza and we could oppose them. However, there were some personal links there, personal collections, and these men would sometimes break into the police station itself and issue threats to the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Budo Obradovic, the president of the Executive Council, was killed in that way? Somebody burst into his office and shot him dead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Did I quote the correct number, 1D3241?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's coming. This is 2341.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, somebody signed on your behalf, but you were put there as the chief of the public security station. We don't have a translation so I will have to read this: On the 20th of November, 1992, at around 2030 hours, at the check -- traffic check-point Butila, Rajlovac municipality, Pero Hrkalovic [phoen] from Rajlovac, under the influence, and with his rifle cocked, approached a group of police officers of this station, or rather, approached Zarko Vidic and Goran Stanisic, asking them why they were checking traffic, telling them that they were thieves and so on and so forth, on which occasion the military police disarmed them. In other words, they called the military police to assist them. On this occasion they were disarmed by the military police, but some 20 or so citizens had gathered and they protested and tried to protect Pero so that members of the police and the military assessed that it was time to withdraw from the check-point to avoid a physical conflict, which they did because the citizens gathered there were armed. The command of the Ilidza Brigade was informed of the incident and this station, in coordination with the military police and the public security station in Rajlovac, took measures in order to establish all the facts relating to this incident. The first question: Is this one of those cases where the state authorities clashed with irregular groups and their erratic behaviour?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what this illustrates. I can only say that there were a number of such incidents. Unfortunately, in some of them, firearms were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question: This report says that these citizens that had gathered there, some 20 of them, were armed. Now, let me ask you, Mr. Glavas, do you recall Tito's doctrine of an armed people and the purpose of that was for them to be able to defend themselves in case of an aggression? This was primarily in reference of the Warsaw Pact, correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, could you tell us -- I mean, can it be said -- or, rather, who is the state representative, a government representative, in this particular instance in this incident? Is it the member -- the police and the army, or the citizens and the people who were opposing them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be the police officers and the army who tried to prevent these incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you feel that it was your responsibility to oppose -- or do you feel responsible for these -- the conduct and the behaviour of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't really say that I feel responsible for that, but this is just a good illustration of how difficult it was to carry out our duties and how dangerous it was to carry out our duties as police officers, of maintaining law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1081, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1562 from the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, Mr. Glavas, in addition to threatening the safety and security of citizens, you also had problems with major incidents involving theft and burglaries and looting. So can we agree that this was a time, the wartime, conducive to all types of criminal offences?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really ask you about what the percentage of psychopaths would be in any society at any given time, especially under these conditions, but we'll leave that to experts. But can I ask you, under these circumstances, was it the case that the individuals who were already prone to crime from before now had an opportunity to reactivate themselves?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let's see what the position of the authorities was on the matter of private property. This is a document from the municipal government of Hadzici, dated the 10th of June, 1992. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see that this is a request to take measures to hand over individuals who failed to report after they received a mobilisation call, in the territory of Hadzici municipality. And then it says that a large number of conscripts failed to report after they were mobilised, and who are now in the territories of Pale, Sokolac and Han Pijesak municipalities but who hail from the Hadzici municipality, and the Hadzici municipality actually wanted those other municipalities to send those people back?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's -- we can see here that there were mass attempts to desert, where people left their areas, their municipalities, for other areas, where the fighting was far less fierce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And we see in the second paragraph that the Serb Municipality of Hadzici wants them to be sent back and put them in use for defence because we are continuously targeted by Muslim Ustasha forces, otherwise we shall label all of those who had left the Serb Municipality of Hadzici as deserters, confiscate their property and forbid their return to the territory of the Serb Municipality of Hadzici. From what you know, was this a reference to the Serb conscripts who actually tried to avoid and who left the municipality in order to avoid being mobilised?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly who it refers to, to Serb conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Aside from this threat that their property would be confiscated, because that is within the jurisdiction of courts, but this is a call, a desperate call, for them to come back and help defend their fatherland; correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1082, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to see 65 ter 1621, please. The 15th of September, so as that document from the military department of Hadzici says, it was only from the 15th of September onwards that communication could be established with the central organs. Let's see what it says here: "Decision has been made by the municipal authorities to rescind rights obtained on the basis of tenancy rights or employment. "Article 1, all persons who were formerly resident on the territory of the Serb Municipality of Hadzici who have not returned to the municipality and have not provided an explanation for their inability to return to the competent municipal authorities for military affairs," and so on and so forth, "shall have the status of displaced persons and shall not have the right to citizenship of Republika Srpska." Does this pertain to persons who fled from Republika Srpska? Or those who were in Pale or some other municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a reference to persons who left the territory of the municipality of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. "Article 2, persons referred to in Article 1 herein have a statutory right to a socially owned flat in the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici shall no longer be entitled to any rights obtained on the basis of tenancy rights." And Article 4: "The property of persons referred to in Article 1 herein shall be provisionally used for the needs of the defence of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici. The competent municipal organs shall oversee the care and manner of use of this property." First, let us make a distinction here. The municipality believes that they are not entitled to socially owned apartments that were made available to them and that they do not actually own?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Property that is not in dispute will be used for defence and it is the competent organs that are going to provide for that, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this pertain to Serbs who don't want to go back to defend the municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. However, I think that the basic reason for making this kind of decision was the fact that in the area of Hadzici, due to reasons well known from before, and due to the situation as such, there were quite a few available apartments and at that time there was an onslaught of refugees. And I think that that is how the municipal authorities were trying to deal with that, how to have those apartments allocated. That's how I interpret this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't know whether you know this but it did appear in the Official Gazette. On the 19th of August, I annulled every possibility to infringe upon property rights. However, the government did prescribe a way in which property would be made temporarily available not to the local population but people who came from elsewhere. That's what you meant when you were speaking of refugees, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1083, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1543? And that's the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a very early decision of the Crisis Staff of the 26th of May, 1992. It's a decision on the establishment of a commission set up to make a list of all abandoned flats and property on the territory of the Hadzici Serb municipality, number 1. On the basis of this decision a commission for making a list of all abandoned flats and property on the territory of the Serb Municipality of Hadzici is being established, and then its members are listed there, and the appointed commission, it says further on, is obliged to make a list of all abandoned flats and property on the territory of the Serb municipality of Hadzici and also to seal them so that they could all be registered and placed at the disposal of the Serb Municipality of Hadzici. See, so a list is being made, they are being sealed. You were there, do you remember that this was done by the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that very well, the time when these apartments were sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any looting going on at the time? Was this measure indispensable, as it were?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, inter alia was a measure of caution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1084, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter number 1645?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from December. This reflects the position of the municipal authorities with regard to property and property-related rights. When you see the essence, we will ask you whether you are in agreement. Can we have page 3? 5, point 5. Item 5, yes, we have it in English now. Yes. The third subparagraph underneath the name of Vitomir Banduka, it says: "The question of whether the commission for allocating flats should allocate private houses was also raised. Ratko Gengo explained that this commission did not allocate flats and houses but provided accommodation for refugees." Then further on, item 6 says: "It is believed that this decision raised a dilemma as to what should be done with the -- with," and we cannot read what it says -- "who had taken shelter outside our municipality because of war operations. Branislav Jovanovic --" it's the next page in English. "Branislav Jovanovic asked for an explanation about what about those who left after the 13th of August, 1992? The answer he received was that they were considered to be refugees from this municipality, to have fled from this municipality." Does this correspond to your knowledge about the ways and means resorted to by the municipality to resolve the problem of accommodating those who arrived in Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of that, but, Mr. Karadzic, I have a small remark to make. I don't mind commenting on this record or these minutes of the Municipal Assembly of Hadzici, that speaks about how certain vital problems were being resolved in the area. I'm accepting this. I accept that I can comment upon what happened there because I believe you won't have any other witnesses from that area. However, I already said that I'm not a person who was ever involved in politics, so I don't think that I'll be able to give you any kind of useful comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I accept that. Can we have page 7? It's probably page 8 in the document. 6442, that's the ERN number. Yes, that's right. That's it in the Serbian language. Just let us have a look at this. As far as looting is concerned, it is believed that there is considerably less of it and that omissions that happened in the initial period are due to the fact that the station was involved in defence. So the members of the station were taking part in fighting, right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that has already been established on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1085, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D3084?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a letter of yours, information that you are sending in your capacity of chief of the security station in the Serb Municipality of Ilidza. Can you read this? Please find attached a report concerning the discovery of shell fuses and gunpowder in gas cylinders; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this case. It's my name and surname there but it was signed by Mr. Nikolic who was my assistant at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the second page now? Since there is a translation, I don't have to read all of it out. Could you please have a look and can you tell us whether this is what happened? Was Dr. Pejic the director of the municipal -- of the military hospital in Blazuj, that took care of our own wounded and those of the other side?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this case, why did he go to the police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard for me to read this. It's barely legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what he says, that he received two cylinders from the UNHCR and they did not contain gas but were filled with a suspicious substance. A commission of the Ilidza Public Security Station, representatives of the military and civilian police attached to UNPROFOR, and one UNHCR representative went to the spot and established the two metal cylinders were involved, one of a net weight of 28.3 kilograms with a certain number and the other one with a net weight of 43.8 kilograms with a number that follows. The gas cylinders were opened by authorised officials and gun powder was found in the first one, but in the other one, 200 fuses were found, most probably for 82-millimetre calibre shells. Have I jogged your memory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I remember the case. I know what this is all about. I know that this was a serious omission, and I think that Dr. Pejic or somebody from the military gave a public interview and we were supposed to deal with this on a confidential basis. We were -- we were almost in a position to find a lot more of such material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1086, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, 1671. That's the 65 ter number. Could we have that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who Dusan Kalajdzic is, commander of the Blazuj reserve police station?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the man. I know him in person -- I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He is reporting, on the 19th of September, 1993, and explaining what was going on. He is speaking about the history of the reserve police station, the public security station in Blazuj. Can we have the next page, please? Mr. Kalajdzic is presenting the history of the division of the MUP. And let us have a look at this other paragraph, the second paragraph. And in English it's the last paragraph on this page, where it says, once Tomo Kovac assumed the duty of commander and so on, from 1991, the SDA leadership of Rakovica, through the municipality and its head, Edin, twice requested in writing, through the municipality chief Edin, that Blazuj station be divided. This was seen for what it was, and pursuant to Tomo's instructions, this was not allowed. Although Edin had asked for that at meetings of commanders, an effort was being made to reinforce the Muslim station in Rakovica. Could I please have the next page in English? Do you remember this was immediately after the multi-party elections? The elections took place in November, and the government was established in mid-January 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have the next page? Now, does this document demonstrate -- this about the barricades is not very important at the moment. Let's move to the paragraph which begins on the 4th of April, 1992. It says that the following actions were taken in -- of intercepting and checking suspicious Muslim vehicles following reports received with weapons at Kobiljaca. Is this proof that immediately after the elections in early 1991, manipulations of the police began with the intention of splitting the MUP and to reinforcing the Muslim police forces?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. But I don't think that it's appropriate for me to comment on this. I said something to that effect to the OTP. This is a chronology of events that took place when I was not there and I was in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, your Excellency, I'm not going to tender this at this point. We shall have to wait for another witness to tender it through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that you will find appropriate people from Ilidza who can be better placed to confirm this than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]
