utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask you briefly about some striking and drastic events that as a policeman you should have been aware of, which took place in your municipality. Can you just confirm whether you know about them, you don't know about them, or maybe you don't know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in March of 1992, the Serbs from Gornja and Donja Rastelica noticed in the melting snow the Muslims digging trenches in the area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and that was nothing unusual for that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that armed Muslim groups that numbered a total of 300 to 400 men, according to some opinions, there were more of them, led by Mirsad Sabic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the names again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you need to repeat your question, starting from the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that there were armed groups numbering a total of 300 to 400 men, led by Mirsad Sabic, Mujo Lihovac [phoen] and his son, Nijaz Lihovac, aka Gera, in accordance with a so-called directive of the TO staff of Efendic, on the 11th of May, encircled the JNA barracks, the Zupa [as interpreted] near Gornji Zovik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we find out what Dr. Karadzic is reading from?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the questions that I'm putting to the witness, either asking him to confirm or to deny, but I can recommend to Ms. Edgerton this book called "The Black Book" by Mr. Toholj, from the information centre, and the book is based on witness statements. And the majority of these witnesses will appear as Defence witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, here we have a policeman who didn't have any political party affiliations and who may have known these things. Mr. Glavas, are you aware of these things?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, I am. Whatever you said is consistent with what I said earlier. We are talking here about members of the reserve police force in this place, Mr. Sabic is well known, but I think that the date is not correct. I think that the Krupa barracks was attacked on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says that it started on the evening, probably continued on the 12th. It says that Zarko Milic and another two soldiers were killed, and also a certain Nijaz Mehic on the side of the attackers. One of the killed JNA soldiers was wounded in the leg and died of haemorrhage on the way to hospital. The others were captured, taken to the forestry building in Tarcin --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters cannot repeat such a long list of names spoken so quickly. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters can't follow with that speed, in particular you're enumerating those names.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. So Vlado Bozic, Dragan Mutavdzija, reservists Dragan Jaksic, Dragan Lojanica, Vojno Milanovic, and Slavomir Vidojevic were first detained at the fire-fighting centre in Tarcin, and then two days later in a silo, which, in that manner, became a mass camp. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am quite familiar with this case. Later, it would turn out that practically these were the only individuals that could enjoy the proper status of prisoners of war. The rest were all civilians. So we are talking here about the people that were only capable of being treated as prisoners of war. The other people were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 17th of May, a raid was carried out in Tarcin and that the remaining Serbs were arrested, and that this action was led -- Slobodan Kukricar was killed, and Nedeljko Vukovic [phoen] and Gane Bozic [phoen] were captured. The attackers were led by Mirsad Bratic; Cedomir Domuz [phoen]; Zijad Imamovic; Mirsad Selimovic, aka Srce; a certain Pisca [phoen], last name Mrdzanic [phoen]; and another Mrdzanic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do. But I'm not sure that you put your question correctly. I think that we mentioned this in the context on the attack on Zunovac [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. You are correct. The first attack on the Zunovnica barracks was carried out on the afternoon of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your time is up. Conclude by 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise to the interpreters. We have a wonderful opportunity to ask this of the man who, by virtue of his position, could have known all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the village of Kasetici was attacked from the direction of Crepljani five days before the action in Tarcin of 25th of May, that there were five fatalities, and that one day before that, the whole Serbian family consisting of Aso Milosevic, Dejan Milosevic, Jovanka Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's just all going too fast, Your Honour, to allow any of us to properly catch up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm only amazed by the interpreters, the quality of interpreters and the stenographers who are following.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, but I'm pressed for time. That's my problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is it true that the village of Kasetici was attacked from Tarcin, Do, and Dejovici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I am familiar with this case but that was not the sequence of events as you stated. Now, this was an attack on the barracks in Zunovac, and after we recaptured our positions and while the Bosniak forces were retreating, this massacre in Kasetici happened. This was more or less what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the Muslim forces, while retreating, killed the Milosevic family, and the burst of fire were fired by Adem Kalem, Azemi Sakovic [phoen] and their leader was Ahmet Sakovic. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that this incident is soon going to be tried in Republika Srpska because we filed a criminal report because we know exactly who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And these victims were massacred?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were mostly elderly people who were massacred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the Serbs of Rastelica were also the subject of a pogrom when Refik Tufa came with another two men, killed -- arrested all the men and took them towards Tarcin? Do you remember this, being a policeman?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember. You don't need to elaborate these issues. I know very well what this is about. Rastelica was attacked on the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was led by Refik Tufa. Then it says on the 10th of May, the policeman Mirsad Sabic came with another man in escort and ordered the Serbs to hand over their weapons. On the early morning of the 29th, three days after the devastation of Bradina, three lines of Muslim or three circles of Muslim soldiers encircled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the village and this Ferhatovic was among them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, I just let you go, continue, but how relevant are these events at all?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The position of the Defence, Your Excellency, is that the situation in Hadzici was not a regular one in which the state is responsible for what is going on. It was chaos. To begin with, the Muslim side separated themselves, they left the Serbian part of Hadzici, organised themselves, dug trenches, and launched attacks on the barracks and military installations; and on the other hand, the Serbian authorities were unskilled, they were recently formed, and this part of the municipality was flooded by refugees. I want this witness just to confirm whether the state was capable of doing anything because in this particular case, the state was accused of being responsible for certain events. I just want a picture to be portrayed for the benefit of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question is how the facts that the Muslims allegedly committed crime are relevant to your case? Is that the reason why the Serbs committed crime?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My thesis is that the Serbs did not commit crimes because the state and state organs prevented that, but what the Muslims did created certain atmosphere of panic and vengeful behaviour. We have here a representative of the state who was combatting crimes committed both by the Serbs and the Muslims. So I wanted this witness to make a picture for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber does not argue with you. That being the case, such facts are not necessary all the more. Conclude your cross-examination in three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, I would now like to show you a map of Hadzici, a plane geographic map, 65 ter 19107, 65 ter 19107. I believe it would be easier for you to mark on this map the separation line and also the line between the two municipalities, the Serb and the Muslim part of the municipality. The page is 0701-0752 under the number that I gave you, the 65 ter number. From the municipal binder. I would like to ask my learned friend whether we have the right number for the municipal binder, municipality binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's page 31?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I don't have that binder with me but I think Your Honours must be able to assist. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order to mark it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Glavas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karadzic, if you don't have the map, perhaps I can make it easier for you, and I can provide the trig points. It's from the Stupnik-Obeljak elevation point, Brezovaca, Kasatici, by way of Tinovo, Gunsar [phoen], Ostrik. And then towards the border with Croatia or with the Croatians, you have the elevations of Bela and Kokoska. So that was the line, the boundary. I know them by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Croats arrest and detain Serbs, your Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had -- we didn't have any misunderstandings or any conflicts with the Croats who were on the border with Hadzici municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the Serbs in Hadzici? Did they arrest and detain Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe if there were any cases, there were very few.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did Musici inhabitants take part in the attack on Hadzici? And did they open fire in Hadzici in the attack on the barracks, and did they open fire within the town itself?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if they opened fire on the barracks, but I believe that we had information that they had attacked the road -- a road there so that it was difficult to use that road at the time. They opened fire on that road. But I'm not sure about the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now the Court Usher will help you to activate the e-pen and then perhaps you can show us and mark the border between the Serb part of the municipality and the Bosnian part, the boundary of the municipality of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where it says "Municipal Assembly building" and we see these two yellow triangles, is that the very centre? Is that the town itself, Hadzici town?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this part here that I'm indicating. [Marks]. I'm not sure whether this is the border, whether I'm absolutely accurate, but the accurate delineation of the border were the elevations that I mentioned earlier. So we didn't even have 30 per cent of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were the Muslim forces right behind these hills behind Hadzici and they could open fire on you at any time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their forces were on the other side of Ormanje. We were on this side and Ormanje was a sort of buffer zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No man's land?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to that peak of Ormanje, the mountain peak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark the Serb part with an S and the Muslim part with an M?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And would you now please date and sign this document? I believe it's the 16th.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And my final question, Witness: We saw that there were Muslim civilians in the Serb part of the municipality who were on work -- under work obligation and who could freely move around. Now, were there Serbs on the Muslim part of the municipality who were free and remained free until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that perhaps there may have been two to three men, mostly older men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also told us that you -- there was a border with Konjic municipality and was it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's with respect to the redirect. Your Honours haven't inquired yet and, I'm sorry, I haven't offered an estimate of what time I might take, but this is a pattern that repeats itself and the Prosecution is continually constricted with Dr. Karadzic pressing the line by asking one more question, one more question, which usually amounts -- which usually has an effect on our effective redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't expect that your redirect would last more than 20 minutes? You have more than 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but I note it's now 10 after 2.00 and we are sitting until 2.30 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've concluded more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell us about Bradina, did Bradina in any way have any ties to your municipality or did it belong to your municipality, and can you tell us what kind of danger it posed to the Muslims and what happened to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bradina was part of Konjic municipality, but it's a fact that it was closer to the Hadzici municipality area. It was a purely or predominantly Serb-populated municipality, and in my view, in view of the -- of the -- their position militarily they were absolutely unable to pose any danger or threat to the Muslims because on -- they bordered on the one side on the Muslims and then on the other side, they also had borders with territory that was under the control of the Muslims, so they were some sort of buffer zone. And there was not a chance, not even a theoretical chance, that they could actually oppose the Muslims, and unfortunately, a lot of people were arrested there, some of them were taken prisoner and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that some 50 to 60 civilians were buried outside the church grounds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you said you have concluded your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have. Thank you, Mr. Glavas. I would like to tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This marked map will be admitted as Exhibit D1087. Yes, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, I'd like to deal again with some themes that have come up in your cross-examination. The first being one that you spoke about to a great extent today, the presence of paramilitaries in Ilidza. Now, talking about the presence of paramilitaries in Ilidza, Dr. Karadzic asked you at one point that the -- his question was the government authorities actually feared these groups and they tried to avoid getting into contact with them, and he asked you whether that meant that they didn't have at their disposal a sufficient or strong enough police force to deal with them. And your response was, well, that wasn't the only problem. We had a large police force in Ilidza and we could oppose them. However, there were some personal links, personal connections, and these men would sometimes break into the police station itself and issue threats. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm not sure that I said "personal connections." What I meant was there were personal relations. It doesn't mean that they were close with the president of the municipalities. However, there were cases -- well, I, for instance, know of a specific case, that Brne would burst into Mr. Prstojevic's office and pull out his gun, his pistol.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, I'm very curious about these personal connections because you've said, when you were asked whether Prstojevic and Unkovic were the ones who ordered or controlled the paramilitaries, you said, well, that was suspicious information, and you also said that the police had -- and particularly cited Mr. Kovac and his argument with Legija, and that's in your written evidence, you said that the police absolutely did not have anything to do with the paramilitaries being in Ilidza. And when you discussed, in your written evidence, the attempts to rid Ilidza of the paramilitaries, you talked about the cooperation of the Ilidza brigade commander. So who, if the political leaders, the police, and the Ilidza Brigade had nothing to do with the presence of the paramilitaries in Sarajevo, who were the personal connections that ensured their presence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I said this in the interview we had in Sarajevo, how it was possible for paramilitary units to be there. This was true information. So through friendly connections and ties, they were able to come to a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You seem to be well informed. Are you able to give us a name? And perhaps it might be easier if I just confine my question to Ilidza municipality.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I will repeat what I've already said in Sarajevo. When I came to Ilidza, and when I was briefed on the presence of these paramilitary units, I learned, among other things, that Dragisa Ivelja was the one who actually brought in these paramilitary units, and I had very specific information that he was the one who had brought in the Arkan -- Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who ensured the presence of the Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think because at the time they were members of the Serbian Radical Party for all practical purposes, and at this time it was being established in that area as well, I believe that it was members of the Serbian Radical Party who actually ensured or made it possible for them to be present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did the individual whose name you've just given us which reads Dragica Ivelja have any role in the government or the authorities of the Serb municipality of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know whether he had any role in the government or the authorities, but I do know that at the time he was involved in, well, let's -- shall we call it rear activities?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "rear activities"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I meant supplies, logistics, primarily supplies of food for the needs of the citizens of Ilidza. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to another area. You talked with Dr. Karadzic about communications in your cross-examination today. And at page 10 you were asked whether -- in regard to a particular document you were asked whether the local authorities during the first months of the conflict were primarily left to their own devices, and that there was no communication between local and central authorities. That's page 10, line 16 to 20. And you said yes, that's correct. And then you commented on another document, 65 ter 01648, pages 33, lines 24 to 34, there Dr. Karadzic asked in regard to that document whether this confirmed that the information you gave, namely that the central organs could not be reached easily before mid-September, and you said that that confirms that precisely. Do you remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that evidence, but I was referring to the type of communications that we had in terms of communications equipment. It was very poor, so we were only able to report on any incidents or any events of any significance by way of courier service.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So when your answers referred generally to local authorities, were you, in fact, actually limiting your answer specifically to the situation as you recalled it in Hadzici municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And generally, I spoke about matters that had to do with the activities that I had as the chief of police down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In that case, I'd just like to go to one document which you've already seen today, D1073. You were shown that at page 39 of today's transcript. This is a report on the daily -- on daily events by the Minister of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, this is dated 12 May 1995, and if you go down to paragraph 2 of the English on page 1 and just scroll down so you can see further down the same page in Serbian -- pardon me, it's dated 1992, my mistake. You see that this document talks about the situation as it was for the past two days in Hadzici, saying, among other things, despite unequal balance of forces, with the Serbs being less in number, attacks of Muslim paramilitary formations had been resisted successfully. That was not read out to you earlier. And I just want to ask whether this type of report reflects your regular communication through the hierarchy of your organisation to the central authorities.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just go over to another document, please, D00317, which you also saw today. It's a report on the combat readiness of the Serbian Municipality of Hadzici, dated 29 May 1992. And if we could go over to the Serbian page 2 and stay --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could scroll down a little bit, thank you, to the bottom of this page, this document says -- the Serbian page needs to go up a little bit, and he can't see the whole page on the left-hand side so I don't want it to be cut off.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This document says, among other things, that as a result of combat activities, the Crisis Staff -- or we, asked for help from the commander of the HQ of the Main Staff. I see the English doesn't quite match. The English says -- pardon me, the English reads, "Commander of the HQ of the Serbian Republic." And the B/C/S version reads, "Commander of the Main Staff of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina himself, who presently sent a fighting group under the command of Lieutenant-Colonel Petrovic." And I just want to ask you, to your mind, does this reflect an ability of people at the local level in Hadzici to contact the central authorities at a critical time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I'll tell you why. I see here mention of this Lieutenant-Colonel. Now, I was in Hadzici at the time, and his mission, his only mission, was to pull out the conscripts from Pazarici and -- or, rather, the cadets and his primary purpose of his being in Hadzici was that mission. And they were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the second part of his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, could you repeat your second part of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not put the two together and I wouldn't bring that in relation with the local authorities for the simple reason that I know that the then-former Yugoslav People's Army had some loose ends that they had to capture. Among other things, there was a group of cadets in Pazarici barracks, and they had come there in order to pull them out of there. In the meantime, the attack on Hadzici was launched and they happened to be there, so they were able to help us in recapturing Zunovnica and pulling out those cadets from Pazarici and pull them out of that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Glavas you've earlier looked at this document and said it was quite accurate and that was the basis on which I put this document to you. Are you saying that the document is now no longer -- is not accurate, in fact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I meant. Perhaps someone misinterpreted it. I'm sorry. All of a sudden this went away. What you read out to me now is something that I had not known before. However, what I said now is something that can be checked very, very easily. I know the name and surname of this Lieutenant-Colonel who came and I know what his mission was, what the purpose of his coming to our area was. First of all to get the cadets out of the barracks in Pazarici, and that was under the control of the Bosniak forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now you're repeating yourself a little bit. What I read to you was the passage that said, "We asked for help from the commander of the headquarters of the Serbian Republic of --" pardon me. "We asked for help from the commander of the Main Staff of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina himself." Are you saying that that is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who wrote this document. I cannot say now whether it's accurate. I told you, these active duty officers who were in the area at the time were only there for the reasons that I mentioned a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move on to one final area. Dr. Karadzic, at page 48, asked you whether it ever occurred that the Crisis Staff or any other organ of authority, either police or military, issued orders or allowed or tolerated illegal treatment of detainees. And your answer was, well, in principle, there were no such instances. So I'd like to know how to interpret this answer. Are you saying it didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But you've already given evidence about civilians in Hadzici being detained at the sports centre for the express purpose of exchange. You've given evidence of women being among that number. You've given evidence of abuse going on, in fact, in your written evidence you said sexual abuse, at the sports centre, and you've given evidence that the sports centre was instituted and maintained under the control of the Crisis Staff. So how do you explain your answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, are you seeking to impeach the witness, because this is a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. May I answer this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, we will allow you to put the question. Yes, please proceed to answer, Mr. Glavas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Carolyn, it seems that we haven't understood each other. I'm not contesting what you said just now. Those are facts. That is what I said in my statement. It never crossed my mind to deny any of what I had stated to you. I was just trying to say that the municipal authorities and the police authorities and the military authorities never gave any instructions to carry out any kind of torture against persons who were detained on certain premises. I am not challenging the fact that persons were not being brought in and detained in various areas, including where I was chief of police, but that is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's everything, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask for one particular clarification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, this time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will remain unclear, Excellency who are the people who called themselves Seseljevci or Arkanovci, Seselj's men or Arkan's men, and the impression will remain that it is people from came from Serbia. Already in April, these people who had come from Serbia were denied any hospitality and -- well, you ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please, I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Glavas, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I can answer the question, but I think that Mr. Karadzic and I do not agree this time. I had already given a statement to the OTP down there, when I spoke about paramilitary formations. I said that there were these two basic groups, but they can also be mixed. I spoke of para formations that come exclusively from our area, Republika Srpska, and also there were those that came from elsewhere. When I said elsewhere, I meant that these were persons coming from Serbia. That is the statement I made to the Office of the Prosecutor, and I cannot deny that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Glavas, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Tribunal and the Chamber, I thank you very much for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just for one moment. If I could ask that eight different passages from our transcript be made public in connection with Mr. Zecevic's situation. I've given the dates to your staff and if we could also make that part of the public record I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There seems to be no reason not to grant your request, but just out of an abundance of caution, the Chamber will consider each transcript and will give its ruling in writing in due course. And tomorrow, we will be hearing Mr. Pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, the first witness is scheduled to testify by videolink and he's testifying under pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And the other witness is available in The Hague too ---

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- to commence as soon as the other one is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for the delay but the hearing is now adjourned for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of February 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.33 p.m.,
